quests.passage: Doing the same twenty-minute commute every day for ten years felt monotonous to him.
quests.question: boring because it stays exactly the same with no variety
quests.hint: Think about why ten years of the identical drive would wear on someone.
quests.explanation: 'Monotonous' describes something dull because it never varies. Ten years of the exact same commute is a strong example of that kind of tedium.
quests.wordInContext: The factory job was monotonous, the same three movements repeated all shift long.

quests.passage: Her morning routine never changed: coffee first, then a quick check of the news before work.
quests.question: a fixed, regular sequence of actions someone follows
quests.hint: Notice the phrase 'never changed' and the order she follows each day.
quests.explanation: 'Routine' describes a set pattern of actions repeated regularly, usually in the same order. Coffee, then news, every morning, is exactly this kind of fixed sequence.
quests.wordInContext: His evening routine included a short walk and locking the front door twice.

quests.passage: The weather this spring has been unpredictable, sunny one hour and pouring rain the next.
quests.question: changing in ways that are hard to guess in advance
quests.hint: Look at how quickly the weather swings from one extreme to another.
quests.explanation: 'Unpredictable' describes something that keeps changing in ways nobody can foresee. Sun switching to heavy rain within an hour shows how little anyone can rely on this spring's forecast.
quests.wordInContext: Stock prices can be unpredictable, rising and falling for no obvious reason.

quests.passage: His erratic sleep schedule meant he might be awake at 3 a.m. one night and asleep by 8 p.m. the next.
quests.question: irregular and inconsistent, without a stable pattern
quests.hint: Notice that unpredictable weather is about not knowing what's coming; this is about a pattern that keeps breaking itself.
quests.explanation: 'Erratic' describes behavior that shifts inconsistently, with no stable routine to rely on. Swinging between 3 a.m. and 8 p.m. bedtimes shows there's no fixed pattern at all.
quests.wordInContext: The bus service became erratic during the strike, sometimes arriving early and sometimes not at all.

quests.passage: Their neighbor was predictable, watering his lawn at exactly six o'clock every single evening.
quests.question: behaving in a way that can be expected in advance, without surprises
quests.hint: Think about how you could set your watch by this neighbor's habit.
quests.explanation: 'Predictable' describes behavior so consistent that others can expect it in advance. Watering the lawn at exactly six every evening is about as predictable as a habit gets.
quests.wordInContext: The ending of the movie was predictable long before the final scene.

quests.passage: His habitual late-night snacking was something he had been trying to break for months.
quests.question: done so often that it has become automatic, almost without thinking
quests.hint: Notice that this isn't just something he does — it's something he's actively trying to stop.
quests.explanation: 'Habitual' describes an action repeated so many times it becomes nearly automatic. Trying for months to stop the snacking shows how deeply ingrained the habit has become.
quests.wordInContext: Her habitual nail-biting got worse whenever she felt stressed about exams.

quests.passage: He tends to procrastinate on essays until the night before they are due.
quests.question: to delay doing something that needs to be done
quests.hint: Think about when he actually starts the essay compared to when it's assigned.
quests.explanation: 'Procrastinate' means putting off a task, usually one you should be starting sooner. Waiting until the night before it's due is a classic sign of this delay.
quests.wordInContext: She always procrastinates on cleaning the garage until guests are about to arrive.

quests.passage: It took a second reading before she could truly comprehend the professor's argument.
quests.question: to fully understand the meaning of something
quests.hint: Notice that one reading wasn't enough for the meaning to sink in.
quests.explanation: 'Comprehend' means to grasp the full meaning of something, not just recognize the words. Needing a second reading shows the first wasn't enough for real understanding.
quests.wordInContext: The instructions were so confusing that even the technician struggled to comprehend them.

quests.passage: The actor had to memorize nearly forty pages of dialogue before opening night.
quests.question: to learn something so well that you can recall it exactly, without looking
quests.hint: Think about what the actor needs to be able to do on stage without a script in hand.
quests.explanation: 'Memorize' means committing something to memory so it can be recalled perfectly later. Forty pages of dialogue with no script on stage requires exactly this kind of recall.
quests.wordInContext: Students had to memorize the periodic table before the chemistry exam.

quests.passage: The charity built schools in villages where most adults had remained illiterate their whole lives.
quests.question: unable to read or write
quests.hint: Think about why building schools would matter so much for these particular villages.
quests.explanation: 'Illiterate' describes someone who has never learned to read or write. Villages where most adults never gained this skill are exactly where such schools are needed most.
quests.wordInContext: Nearly a fifth of the population was illiterate before the government's education program began.

quests.passage: The teacher asked him to elaborate on his answer instead of just giving a one-word reply.
quests.question: to give more detail or explanation about something already said
quests.hint: Notice what the teacher wanted instead of the short, one-word answer.
quests.explanation: 'Elaborate' means adding more detail to something already mentioned. Being asked for more than a one-word reply is a direct request to elaborate.
quests.wordInContext: The witness was asked to elaborate on what she saw right before the accident.

quests.passage: Even as a young student, she was remarkably articulate when presenting her project to the class.
quests.question: able to express ideas clearly and effectively in speech
quests.hint: Think about how clearly she could get her ideas across, despite her age.
quests.explanation: 'Articulate' describes speaking in a way that expresses ideas clearly and well. Presenting a project clearly, even at a young age, shows unusually strong articulation.
quests.wordInContext: The new spokesperson was articulate under pressure, never fumbling a single question from reporters.

quests.passage: The front-desk job required her to multitask, answering calls while checking guests in at the same time.
quests.question: to do more than one task at the same time
quests.hint: Notice the two separate jobs she's doing at once.
quests.explanation: 'Multitask' means handling multiple tasks simultaneously instead of one at a time. Answering calls while checking in guests is a clear case of doing two things at once.
quests.wordInContext: Working as a barista taught him to multitask, taking orders while pulling shots and calling out names.

quests.passage: A good manager knows how to delegate tasks instead of trying to do everything alone.
quests.question: to give part of your work or responsibility to someone else
quests.hint: Think about what the alternative to doing everything alone would be.
quests.explanation: 'Delegate' means passing tasks or responsibility to other people rather than handling everything yourself. Avoiding the trap of doing it all alone is exactly what delegating solves.
quests.wordInContext: The project failed because the team leader refused to delegate any part of it.

quests.passage: She managed to negotiate a higher salary before accepting the new position.
quests.question: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement, often involving compromise
quests.hint: Notice that the salary wasn't simply offered — she had to work to change it.
quests.explanation: 'Negotiate' means discussing terms back and forth until both sides agree. Getting a higher salary before accepting the job shows she didn't just accept the first offer.
quests.wordInContext: The two companies spent weeks negotiating the terms of the merger.

quests.passage: With three deadlines in one week, he had to prioritize which report needed his attention first.
quests.question: to decide which tasks are most important and deal with them first
quests.hint: Think about why he can't just work on all three reports at once.
quests.explanation: 'Prioritize' means ranking tasks by importance and handling the most urgent ones first. Deciding which report comes first, with three deadlines colliding, is exactly this kind of ranking.
quests.wordInContext: She had to prioritize her health over her work schedule after the doctor's warning.

quests.passage: The overworked staff finally spoke up after being asked to cover three extra shifts in one week.
quests.question: made to work too much, beyond a reasonable amount
quests.hint: Notice what pushed the staff to finally say something.
quests.explanation: 'Overworked' describes being made to do far more work than is reasonable. Three extra shifts in a single week is a clear sign the staff had been pushed too hard.
quests.wordInContext: The overworked interns were pulling twelve-hour days without any extra pay.

quests.passage: Teachers in the survey often described feeling underpaid given the long hours the job demanded.
quests.question: paid less money than a job or effort deserves
quests.hint: Compare the hours teachers describe working to how they feel about their pay.
quests.explanation: 'Underpaid' describes earning less than the work actually justifies. Long hours paired with low pay is exactly the mismatch this word describes.
quests.wordInContext: Entry-level workers in the industry are often underpaid despite handling significant responsibility.

quests.passage: Their itinerary listed three cities in ten days, with barely a free afternoon in between.
quests.question: a detailed plan of a journey, listing places and times
quests.hint: Think about what kind of document would list three cities and specific days like this.
quests.explanation: 'Itinerary' describes a planned schedule for a trip, showing where and when you'll be. Listing three cities across ten days is exactly the kind of detail an itinerary contains.
quests.wordInContext: Before the tour started, everyone received a printed itinerary with hotel names and departure times.

quests.passage: Roadworks forced drivers onto a long detour that added forty minutes to the usual route.
quests.question: a longer or different route taken to avoid an obstacle on the usual path
quests.hint: Notice why drivers couldn't simply take their normal road this time.
quests.explanation: 'Detour' describes an alternate path taken when the usual route is blocked. Roadworks forcing a longer route, adding forty minutes, is a textbook detour.
quests.wordInContext: A fallen tree forced hikers to take a steep detour around the blocked trail.

quests.passage: Traffic congestion near the stadium made the twenty-minute drive take almost two hours.
quests.question: a state of being overly crowded, causing slow movement
quests.hint: Think about how much the drive time changed because of too many vehicles on the road.
quests.explanation: 'Congestion' describes an overcrowded state that slows everything down, especially traffic. A twenty-minute drive stretching to two hours shows how severe the congestion was.
quests.wordInContext: Congestion at the border crossing left trucks waiting for over six hours.

quests.passage: They planned a two-day stopover in Istanbul before continuing on to their final destination.
quests.question: a short stay at a place partway through a longer journey
quests.hint: Notice that Istanbul wasn't the final destination — just a stop on the way.
quests.explanation: 'Stopover' describes a brief stay somewhere during a longer trip, before continuing on. Two days in Istanbul, with the real destination still ahead, is exactly this kind of pause.
quests.wordInContext: Their flight included a six-hour stopover in Doha, just enough time to grab dinner at the airport.

quests.passage: Their flight was delayed by three hours because of a storm over the coast.
quests.question: made to happen later than originally planned
quests.hint: Think about what caused this flight to leave later than scheduled.
quests.explanation: 'Delayed' describes something pushed back from its original time. A storm forcing a three-hour wait is a clear cause of that delay.
quests.wordInContext: The package was delayed at customs for almost a week before it finally arrived.

quests.passage: She spent a whole summer backpacking through three countries, staying in hostels along the way.
quests.question: traveling, usually cheaply, while carrying your belongings in a backpack
quests.hint: Notice the style of travel described — hostels, a backpack, moving between countries.
quests.explanation: 'Backpacking' describes budget travel with your belongings carried in a backpack, often moving between destinations and staying in hostels. Three countries and hostel stays over a summer fit this style of travel exactly.
quests.wordInContext: After university, he went backpacking across South America with nothing but a tent and a guidebook.

quests.passage: After the argument, he became estranged from his brother for almost five years.
quests.question: no longer close to or in contact with someone, often after a conflict
quests.hint: Think about what caused the distance between the brothers and how long it lasted.
quests.explanation: 'Estranged' describes a relationship broken by distance or conflict, often between family members. Five years without contact after an argument shows a serious, lasting rift.
quests.wordInContext: She reconnected with her estranged father only after he became seriously ill.

quests.passage: Her strict upbringing meant she learned to cook and clean long before most of her friends did.
quests.question: the way a child is raised and the values or habits they are taught
quests.hint: Notice how her childhood experience compares to that of her friends.
quests.explanation: 'Upbringing' describes how a person was raised, including the habits and expectations instilled early on. Learning chores earlier than her friends reflects the strictness of hers.
quests.wordInContext: His relaxed upbringing meant he never learned to manage money until he lived on his own.

quests.passage: As the only sibling without children of her own, she became the favorite aunt at every gathering.
quests.question: a brother or sister
quests.hint: Think about her relationship to the other people in her family who do have children.
quests.explanation: 'Sibling' refers to a brother or sister. Being singled out as the only one in her family without kids marks her as one of several siblings.
quests.wordInContext: Growing up as the youngest sibling, he was always the last to get a turn choosing the movie.

quests.passage: After the surgery, he was fully dependent on his daughter for meals and daily errands.
quests.question: needing someone else's help or support in order to manage
quests.hint: Notice what he can no longer do without his daughter's help.
quests.explanation: 'Dependent' describes relying on someone else for support or care. Needing his daughter for meals and errands after surgery shows this reliance clearly.
quests.wordInContext: The young plant was still dependent on daily watering until its roots grew stronger.

quests.passage: Her overprotective father called three times during her first solo trip to another city.
quests.question: excessively concerned with keeping someone safe, more than necessary
quests.hint: Think about whether three calls during one trip seems like a normal amount of concern.
quests.explanation: 'Overprotective' describes guarding someone far beyond what the situation calls for. Calling three times during a single trip suggests worry well past the ordinary amount.
quests.wordInContext: Their overprotective coach wouldn't let anyone play again until a doctor cleared every bruise.

quests.passage: He felt resentful after years of being compared to his more successful older sister.
quests.question: feeling bitter or angry about something perceived as unfair, often held onto over time
quests.hint: Notice how long this feeling has been building, and why.
quests.explanation: 'Resentful' describes lingering bitterness, usually over something felt to be unfair. Years of unwanted comparison to a sibling is exactly the kind of situation that builds this feeling.
quests.wordInContext: She grew resentful of always being asked to cover her coworker's unfinished tasks.
